newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to seek fiscal reform and recovery -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to seek fiscal reform and recovery -- MOF.

text.p: Japan's vice finance minister for international affairs, Takatoshi Kato, told a news conference on Tuesday that Japan will pursue fiscal reforms and economic recovery simultaneously.

Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, also told the same news conference that Japan's position of ensuring economic recovery led by domestic demand was unchanged.

Earlier, U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers told reporters he had received an assurance from Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka that Japan would take measures as needed to ensure such growth.

Asked how Mitsuzuka's response corresponded with Japan's tight fiscal policy, Kato said: "The Japanese government's stance and its challenge is to pursue fiscal reforms and economic recovery simultaneously."
Kato added that he thought Mitsuzuka had told Summers similar things in his own words during a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of a "Six Markets" gathering in Tokyo.
Kato did not attend the bilateral meeting.
Sakakibara, who attended the meeting, told the news conference: "Our policy has been to ensure a recovery led by domestic demand. There is no change in our position."
Kato also said that the six economies agreed on the importance of keeping close cooperation in currency markets, economic matters, capital flows, and supervision of financial firms.
They also decided to hold the meeting regularly and agreed to hold another meeting a year from now in Singapore.
Sakakibara also said Japan's current account surplus was likely to continue to decline due to structural changes.

He said significant changes were occuring in the structure of Japan's exports and imports and added: "Taking into account such structural changes, it is unlikely that Japan's current account surplus will increase significantly."
